what: Continuous Exposures via shift() and scale_tx()
title: Modified Treatment Policies & DR-Learner CATE
text: Use shift(delta) additive policies d(,w)=+δd(, w) = + \delta scale_tx(factor) multiplicative policies d(,w)=⋅factord(, w) = \cdot \text{factor}. Internally, tidytmle estimates treatment density ratio nonparametrically using stacked cross-validated classification workflows without parametric normality assumptions:
code: library(tidytmle)  df_cont <- sim_causal_cohort(   n = 350,   outcome_type = "continuous",   treatment_type = "continuous",   seed = 202 ) truth_cont <- attr(df_cont, "truth")  fit_shift <- tmle_spec(   outcome    = y,   treatment  = a,   covariates = c(age, sex, starts_with("lab_")),   estimand   = shift(1.0) ) |>   set_resamples(v_folds = 4L) |>   fit(data = df_cont)  tidy(fit_shift) #> # A tibble: 1 × 8 #>   estimand term     estimate std.error statistic   p.value conf.low #>   <chr>    <chr>       <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1 shift(1) shift(1)     4.86     0.183      26.6 1.13e-155     4.50 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: conf.high <dbl> truth_cont$true_shift_1 #> [1] 4.686838

title: Modified Treatment Policies & DR-Learner CATE
text: Feed cross-fitted Efficient Influence Function pseudo-outcomes binary-treatment tmle_fit directly fit_cate() estimate individual-level treatment effects τ̂(V)\hat{\tau}(V), evaluate Best Linear Projection heterogeneity tests via tidy(), predict onto new cohorts via predict(), quantify uplift ranking via qini_auc():
code: df_het <- sim_causal_cohort(n = 400, outcome_type = "continuous", seed = 303) truth_het <- attr(df_het, "truth")  fit_ate <- tmle_spec(   outcome    = y,   treatment  = a,   covariates = c(age, sex, starts_with("lab_")) ) |>   set_resamples(v_folds = 4L) |>   fit(data = df_het)  cate <- fit_cate(fit_ate, covariates = c(age, sex, lab_1, lab_2, lab_3), v_folds = 4L) tidy(cate) #> # A tibble: 2 × 7 #>   term         estimate std.error statistic  p.value conf.low conf.high #>   <chr>           <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 ATE (BLP In…    1.64      0.127     12.9  5.52e-32    1.39       1.89 #> 2 Heterogenei…    0.921     0.137      6.74 5.49e-11    0.652      1.19 qini_auc(cate) #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   .metric  .estimator .estimate #>   <chr>    <chr>          <dbl> #> 1 qini_auc standard       0.236 #> 2 auuc     standard       1.05  aug_cate <- augment(cate) cor(aug_cate$.cate, truth_het$true_cate) #> [1] 0.8414011

title: Get started with tidytmle
text: Level 1, pass outcome, treatment, covariates (via tidyselect), one causal estimands tmle_spec(), call fit(). Ten-fold cross-fitting, ensemble Super Learner library (glm, glmnet, ranger), adaptive positivity bounds, bounded canonical logistic fluctuation enabled automatically:
code: library(tidytmle)  cohort <- sim_causal_cohort(n = 350, outcome_type = "binary", seed = 42) truth <- attr(cohort, "truth")  fit <- tmle_spec(   outcome    = y,   treatment  = a,   covariates = c(age, sex, starts_with("lab_")),   estimand   = c("ate", "rr", "or") ) |>   set_resamples(v_folds = 5L) |>   fit(data = cohort)  fit #>  #> ── TMLE Fit Summary ── #>  #> n = 350 (observed = 350) | 5-fold CV-TMLE | logistic fluctuation | #> 1.80s #>  #> ── Causal Estimates  #> ATE est = 0.1071 (SE = 0.0511) 95% CI [0.0069, 0.2074] p = 0.0362 #> RR est = 1.3295 (SE = 0.1427) 95% CI [1.0051, 1.7587] p = 0.0460 #> OR est = 1.5805 (SE = 0.2233) 95% CI [1.0202, 2.4484] p = 0.0404 #>  #> ── Nuisance Super Learners  #> Q Super Learner: AUC = 0.713 (weights: glmnet 0.34, glm 0.34, ranger #> 0.33) #> g Super Learner: AUC = 0.623 (weights: ranger 0.33, glm 0.33, glmnet #> 0.33) #>  #> ── Diagnostics  #> ✔ All checks healthy: mean EIF = 5.13e-14, truncated = 0.0%, max EIF leverage = 4.2%.

text: cross-fitted --fold nuisance predictions (Qn0Q_n^0, gng_n, CnC_n) cached inside tmle_fit object, can test stricter positivity bounds, switch estimands ("att", "atc"), target subgroups milliseconds without refitting machine learning models:
code: fit_strict <- retarget(fit, g_bounds = c(0.05, 0.95)) fit_att    <- retarget(fit, estimand = "att") fit_older  <- retarget(fit, subgroup = age >= 55)  dplyr::bind_rows(   dplyr::mutate(tidy(fit), scenario = "Adaptive bounds (All)"),   dplyr::mutate(tidy(fit_strict), scenario = "Strict bounds [0.05, 0.95]"),   dplyr::mutate(tidy(fit_att), scenario = "ATT"),   dplyr::mutate(tidy(fit_older), scenario = "Subgroup age >= 55") ) |>   dplyr::select(scenario, estimand, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high) #> # A tibble: 10 × 6 #>    scenario              estimand estimate std.error conf.low conf.high #>    <chr>                 <chr>       <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> #>  1 Adaptive bounds (All) ate         0.107    0.0511  0.00690     0.207 #>  2 Adaptive bounds (All) rr          1.33     0.143   1.01        1.76  #>  3 Adaptive bounds (All) or          1.58     0.223   1.02        2.45  #>  4 Strict bounds [0.05,… ate         0.107    0.0511  0.00690     0.207 #>  5 Strict bounds [0.05,… rr          1.33     0.143   1.01        1.76  #>  6 Strict bounds [0.05,… or          1.58     0.223   1.02        2.45  #>  7 ATT                   att         0.120    0.0539  0.0142      0.225 #>  8 Subgroup age >= 55    ate         0.209    0.0792  0.0540      0.364 #>  9 Subgroup age >= 55    rr          1.56     0.189   1.08        2.26  #> 10 Subgroup age >= 55    or          2.34     0.334   1.22        4.51

what: Role-Aware Recipe Splitting & workflow_set Super Learning
title: Composing Workflows, Recipes, and Guardrails
text: common source subtle bugs manual causal ML pipelines accidentally leaking treatment column AA cluster ID propensity model g(W)g(W) reusing single recipe(y ~ ., data = df). tidytmle automatically clones adapts preprocessing recipe per nuisance factor (Q, g, C), guaranteeing AA retained Q(,W)Q(, W) C(,W)C(, W) strictly excluded gg’s predictors:
code: library(tidytmle) library(recipes) #> Warning: package 'recipes' was built under R version 4.5.2 library(parsnip) #> Warning: package 'parsnip' was built under R version 4.5.2 library(workflowsets)  df <- sim_causal_cohort(   n = 350,   outcome_type = "continuous",   censoring_rate = 0.15,   n_clusters = 15L,   seed = 101 )  base_rec <- recipe(y ~ ., data = df) |>   step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) |>   step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>   step_zv(all_predictors())  q_wf_set <- workflow_set(   preproc = list(base = base_rec),   models = list(     glm = linear_reg() |> set_engine("glm"),     enet = linear_reg(penalty = 0.05, mixture = 0.5) |> set_engine("glmnet")   ) )  g_spec <- logistic_reg() |> set_engine("glm")  fit_l2 <- tmle_spec(   outcome    = y,   treatment  = a,   covariates = c(age, sex, starts_with("lab_")),   censoring  = delta,   id         = clinic_id,   estimand   = "ate" ) |>   set_preprocessing(base_rec) |>   set_outcome_learners(q_wf_set) |>   set_treatment_learners(g_spec) |>   set_resamples(v_folds = 5L) |>   fit(data = df)  fit_l2 #>  #> ── TMLE Fit Summary ── #>  #> n = 350 (observed = 280) | 5-fold CV-TMLE | logistic fluctuation | #> 2.29s | 15 clusters #>  #> ── Causal Estimates  #> ATE est = 1.7176 (SE = 0.1230) 95% CI [1.4766, 1.9586] p = < 0.0001 #>  #> ── Nuisance Super Learners  #> Q Super Learner: R2 = 0.664 (weights: base_glm 1.00) #> g Super Learner: AUC = 0.604 (weights: logistic_reg_glm 1.00) #> C Super Learner: AUC = 0.660 (weights: glmnet 0.34, glm 0.33, ranger #> 0.33) #>  #> ── Diagnostics  #> ✔ All checks healthy: mean EIF = -4.42e-15, truncated = 0.6%, max EIF leverage = 2.8%.

title: Composing Workflows, Recipes, and Guardrails
text: outcome contains missing values (NA) censoring omitted, tidytmle automatically creates observation indicator Δ=𝕀(¬.na(Y))\Delta = \mathbb{}(\neg\text{.na}(Y)) models informative missingness C(,W)=P(Δ=1∣,W)C(, W) = P(\Delta = 1 \mid , W) rather silently dropping incomplete rows. Native hardhat::importance_weights() hardhat::frequency_weights() likewise propagated nuisance workflows cluster-robust EIF variance estimator:
code: df_miss <- dplyr::select(df, -delta) df_miss$survey_wt <- hardhat::importance_weights(runif(nrow(df_miss), 0.7, 1.5))  fit_auto_c <- tmle_spec(   outcome    = y,   treatment  = a,   covariates = c(age, sex, starts_with("lab_")),   id         = clinic_id,   weights    = survey_wt ) |>   set_resamples(v_folds = 5L) |>   fit(data = df_miss) #> ! Detected 70 missing outcomes (20%); automatically introducing missingness indicator .delta and modeling C(A, W) = P(Delta = 1 | A, W) instead of listwise deletion.  glance(fit_auto_c) #> # A tibble: 1 × 19 #>       n n_observed n_clusters v_folds cv_tmle epsilon  mean_eif #>   <int>      <int>      <int>   <int> <lgl>     <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1   350        280         15       5 TRUE     0.0283 -1.86e-16 #> # ℹ 12 more variables: plugin_vs_tmle_shift <dbl>, g_min <dbl>, #> #   g_max <dbl>, g_bound_low <dbl>, g_bound_high <dbl>, #> #   pct_truncated <dbl>, ess_treated <dbl>, ess_control <dbl>, #> #   max_eif_leverage <dbl>, q_metric <dbl>, g_auc <dbl>, #> #   g_log_loss <dbl> autoplot(fit_auto_c, type = "balance")

what: Diagnostic Plots for a TMLE Fit — autoplot.tmle_fit
title: Diagnostic Plots for a TMLE Fit — autoplot.tmle_fit
text: Produces ggplot2 causal diagnostics fitted "tmle_fit" object: "overlap": Mirrored propensity score density treatment arm g_bounds truncation lines (density-ratio distribution LMTPs). "learners": Cross-validated nuisance performance Super Learner metalearner weights. "eif": Observation-level Efficient Influence Function leverage plot highlighting extreme single-row influence outliers. "sensitivity": Instantaneous retarget() sweep across positivity bounds g_grid showing stability point estimate, 95% CI, truncation rate. "balance": Weighted Love plot comparing unadjusted vs IPW/TMLE-weighted absolute standardized mean differences across baseline covariates.

Strongly recommended (TRUE default) preserve valid influence-function standard errors without Donsker assumptions. g_bounds Positivity truncation rule propensity scores: "adaptive" (Gruber & van der Laan \(5 / (\sqrt{n_{\text{eff}}} \ln n_{\text{eff}})\) bounded [0.01, 0.15]), single numeric threshold b giving [b, 1 - b], length-2 numeric vector c(low, high) (0, 1). fluctuation Fluctuation submodel: "logistic" (bounded canonical logistic fluctuation scaled [0, 1] outcomes — default), "linear" (weighted linear fluctuation), "none" (one-step / plug-without targeting step). max_iter Maximum iterative TMLE steps (reserved iterative updates). tol Convergence tolerance mean EIF. save_nuisance Memory policy nuisance models fitting: "predictions" (default; keeps --fold predictions, CV risk, Super Learner weights instant retarget() minimal RAM), "butcher" (strips heavy internals via butcher::butcher()), "full" (retains full fitted workflows). parallel Logical; TRUE mirai daemons active (mirai::daemons_set()), distributes (fold x learner) tasks via mirai::mirai_map().

title: Specify a Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation (TMLE) Pipeline — tmle_spec
text: outcome Tidyselect specification outcome column. May numeric (continuous 0/1 binary) 2-level factor/logical. treatment Tidyselect specification treatment/exposure column. standard causal estimands ("ate", "att", "atc", "rr", "", "ey1", "ey0"), must binary (0/1, logical, 2-level factor). Modified Treatment Policies (shift(), scale_tx()), numeric continuous. covariates Optional tidyselect specification baseline confounders \(W\). Defaults NULL, automatically selects columns data outcome, treatment, censoring, id, weights. censoring Optional tidyselect specification observation/non-censoring indicator \(\Delta \\{0, 1\}\) (1 = observed, 0 = censored). omitted outcome contains NAs, tidytmle automatically introduces \(\Delta = \mathbb{}(\neg\text{.na}(Y))\) models informative missingness via \(C(, W) = P(\Delta = 1 \mid , W)\). id Optional tidyselect specification clustering/grouping identifier. Automatically triggers grouped cross-validation cluster-robust influence-function standard errors. weights Optional tidyselect specification case-weights column (supporting hardhat::importance_weights(), hardhat::frequency_weights(), positive numeric vectors). estimand Causal estimand(s) target: one "ate", "att", "atc", "rr", "", "ey1", "ey0", Modified Treatment Policy created shift() scale_tx(). Defaults "ate".

title: tidytmle 0.1.0
text: Initial release tidytmle, cross-fitted Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation (TMLE) orchestrator tidymodels ecosystem. Added progressive-disclosure specification API (tmle_spec(), set_preprocessing(), set_outcome_learners(), set_treatment_learners(), set_censoring_learners(), set_resamples(), set_targeting()) accepting parsnip specs, workflows, workflowsets::workflow_set objects. Added role-aware recipes splitting (split_causal_recipes()), automatic informative-missingness modeling (C(, W)), smart stratified/grouped rsample cross-fitting, native hardhat case weights support. Added bounded canonical logistic fluctuation, adaptive positivity truncation, joint EIF inference across "ate", "rr", "", "ey1", "ey0", "att", "atc", cluster-robust EIF SEs, simultaneous uniform confidence bands, VanderWeele-Ding E-values. Added instantaneous retarget() without ML refitting, shift() / scale_tx() Modified Treatment Policies, DR-Learner CATE estimation (fit_cate(), qini_auc()), autoplot() diagnostics ("overlap", "learners", "eif", "sensitivity", "balance").
